description: A reverb built as a five by five mesh of waveguides, each with a frequency of its own

params.text: Picks the pattern of early reflections heard before the mesh; the change is made when the knob is let go
Sets how loud the early reflections are, 0 to 1
Sets how much of the mesh is fed back into itself, 0 to 1; higher settings give a longer tail
Sets how much reverb is heard against the untouched signal, 0 to 1
Scales both mesh frequency jacks before they are added to the mesh knobs, 0 to 100 per cent
Sets the frequency of one point of the mesh, 2Hz to 16384Hz as a power of two; the delay of that waveguide is one cycle at that frequency

inputs.text: Shifts the frequencies of the first sixteen mesh points, one channel of this jack per point, scaled by the Amt knob
Shifts the frequencies of the last nine mesh points, one channel of this jack per point counting from the seventeenth, scaled by the Amt knob
The left signal to be reverberated
The right signal to be reverberated; with nothing patched here the left signal is used for both
Sets that balance by cable in place of the Wet knob, 0-10V across dry to wet
Sets the feedback by cable in place of the FB knob, 0-10V across none to full
Sets the early reflection level by cable in place of the ERAmp knob, 0-10V across none to full

outputs.text: The left output of the mesh
The right output of the mesh

notes: nothing is computed and neither output is written until a cable is patched into InL
with Wet at 0 the mesh is not run at all and the two inputs pass straight through, which is a way to switch the reverb off without unpatching it
the module ships with the standard MVerb settings as factory presets, which are a quicker starting point than the twenty-five mesh knobs
menu: Use Thread — moves the reverb onto a background thread, which keeps it off the audio thread at the cost of some delay
Thread buffer size — sets how many samples that background thread works on at a time; a larger buffer glitches less and delays more
